Review round 2 of spec pose-doctor-recommends-the-commit-graph (a `pose doctor` check and fix, plus a CI step).

Round 1 (run rrn-237e7d9be5f0c4f5, changes-requested) raised F2-F5; account for each in `prior_findings` with the ids the engine's brief lists. Commit 5c1c5658 answers them. F2, F3 and F4 all came from parsing commit-graph files by hand (alternates ignored, a chain preferred to the single graph Git loads first, unsupported or truncated files accepted). Doctor no longer reads those files: `readCommitGraphState` checks `rev-parse --verify --quiet HEAD^{commit}` (failure means not applicable), counts `rev-list --count HEAD`, and from 500 commits runs `git log -1 --format=%H -- <first path of ls-tree HEAD>` with `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT` pointed at a temporary file, then looks for a `bloom`/`statistics` event in which some filter answered (`maybe + definitely_not > 0`). Whatever graph Git loads, by its own rules, is judged. `TestDoctorRecommendsTheCommitGraph` now covers a graph only in an alternate (`clone --shared`) and an unfiltered single graph beside a filtered chain (reported `next`, matching Git). F5: only a missing repository or an unborn HEAD skips the check; any other failure is `warn` with Git's stderr bounded to 200 characters (`TestDoctorCommitGraphReportsAnUnreadableHistory`, with a deleted parent commit). Judge also: whether the first path of HEAD is a sound probe (a path changed in HEAD itself, or only in the root commit, may consult no filter), whether the temporary trace file is safe (created with CreateTemp, removed after), whether a user's own GIT_TRACE2_* settings interfere, and whether an incremental graph that does not cover recent commits is judged sensibly.
